Every effort is made to notify the collector or attending physician if an unlabeled sample is submitted, to allow for timely recollection. 2. An accurate laboratory work-up begins with the proper collection and labeling of patient specimens. Samples should be of adequate quantity, in an appropriate in-date container, and properly labeled. Requirements for most types of specimen collection, types of tubes, and special precautions are listed under the INDEX OF LABORATORY TESTS in this manual. Detailed information can also be accessed in CPRS using "Lab Test Information” in the “Tools” bar. Please contact the laboratory Client Services Unit (ext. 70666) with any questions regarding special collection or handling procedures. 3. Patient Identification Procedures: a. A valid witnessed permit (SF 523) has been obtained (see VANTHCS Memorandum 11-15: Post-mortem Examination). Autopsies are performed at no charge to the family of the deceased. Use leak-proof containers that seal tightly. Avoid spills. c. Minimize direct handling of specimens in transit from the patient to the laboratory. Use sealable biohazard bags to transport the laboratory. The following are key elements that should be included when developing the strategic plan: x The plan should focus on the “Who, What, Where, When and How” of both clinical and business aspects of the Home Telehealth program. x Roles and responsibilities of the team should be well-defined for a successful implementation. x Action items and deadlines should be clearly stated. Information obtained from the needs assessment should guide the plan. 4.2 Home Telehealth Enrollment Goals and Panel Size Home Telehealth Operations Manual - July 2019 Page 12 As part of the process for determining the types of patients that will be enrolled, a decision for panel sizes should be made. community. Currently four to five DMPs are reviewed per quarter. Care Coordinators send issues or requests for revisions to the DMP to the National Telehealth Training Team for review to determine if concerns are safety or non-safety issues. Non-safety issues or revisions will be addressed at the next annual review unless the Home Telehealth Team determines the issue needs to be changed sooner. Care Coordinators will be instructed to initiate a Quality Improvement Request for any issues reported to the National Telehealth Training Team that are determined to be safety issues. Vendors have seven days from the Quality Improvement Request submission date to resolve safety issues. The Home Telehealth community is also notified of the national release of any new VHA DMPs through a VA national alert. All released DMPs are posted on the Connected Care/Telehealth Services web page. The Home Telehealth community is notified of revisions to DMPs for the annual review through a VA national alert. Locations to be evaluated more favorably remain unchanged in Section M5(3)b.(3)c. 30 Form J.9 indicates that Offeror is to describe capability and capacity to deliver products similar to the type and complexity of the tasks. The current form asks for work performed by the current team, however there is no requirement in the form to provide information on the number and types of total resources (capacity) that were delivered to the project. a) How will the US Navy evaluate capacity based on the criteria in the J.9 Form? b) Will the US Navy revise the form to clarify the evaluation criteria? Please see revised Section M and Attachment J.9 via Amendment 0003. 31 The US Navy emphasizes cost reimbursable work for NAVFAC in the AOR even though environmental remediation expertise is largely independent of contract type. Will the US Navy add a section to the proposal for offeror's to discus their historical depth and breadth of cost reimbursable experience as a means of demonstrating cost reimburseable work? Additional sections will not be added to the Solicitation. Solicitation No. N62742-26-R-1801, Small Business Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract for Environmental Remedial Action for Sites in Hawaii, Guam,

elivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract for Environmental Remedial Action for Sites in Hawaii, Guam, and Other Areas within the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Pacific Area of Responsibility QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS 32 When viewed collectively, a number of the solicitation requirements appear to be structured in a manner that disproportionately benefits the incumbent contractor. As a result, it is difficult to justify the substantial cost associated with preparing a high-quality IDIQ proposal when the likelihood of meaningful competition appears limited. If NAVFAC intends to foster a competitive procurement environment, the evaluation criteria should provide a fair opportunity for qualified firms to compete, rather than emphasizing requirements that align primarily with the incumbent’s existing contract performance and experience. Please see revised Section M via Amendment 0003. 33 We are concerned that the J.8 and J.9 forms present an unfair advantage to the incumbent as their projects on the current program will meet all relevant criteria and their "Key Personnel Assigned for Duration of Project/Contract" will show near perfect lacing between Key Personnel and projects. listed objective in the PWS for storefront graphics using perforated window film contract. The QASP provides a systematic method to evaluate the services the contractor is required to furnish. This QASP is based on the premise the Government desires to receive quality product and installation and durability storefront glass graphics using perforated window film and that a service contract to provide this support is the best means of achieving that objective. The contractor, and not the Government, is responsible for management and quality control actions to meet the terms of the contract. The role of the Government is quality assurance to ensure contract standards are achieved. In this contract the quality control program is the driver for product quality. The contractor is required to develop a comprehensive program of inspections and monitoring actions. The first major step to ensuring a “self-correcting” contract is to ensure that the quality control program provides the measures needed to lead the contractor to success. Once the quality control program is approved, careful application of the process and standards presented in the remainder of this document will ensure a robust quality assurance program. deliverables_scope.text: ===== FILE: files/Attachment_1-PWS_-_Deep_Cleaning_Service-FINAL.pdf ===== Performance Work Statement (PWS) Deep Cleaning Services for Base Fitness Centers 1.0 Introduction & Background This Performance Work Statement outlines the requirements for a one-time, non-personal services contract to provide deep cleaning for three fitness facilities: Fitness Center 1, Fitness Center 2, and the Aerobic Center. The Government requires a clean, sanitary, and safe environment for all facility users. 1.1 Definition of Deep Clean Execution of specialized deep cleaning protocols, including heavy-duty machine scrubbing of rubber athletic flooring, VCT stripping and waxing, and hot-water carpet extraction. Comprehensive sanitation, detailing, and soil removal for high-traffic restrooms, locker rooms, entrances, and tile/grout surfaces: • Hard Floors: Must be free of all visible dirt, dust,

rd Floors: Must be free of all visible dirt, dust, grime, and scuff marks, with clean grout lines, corners, and edges. • Rubberized Floors: Must be clean, sanitized, and free of dirt, dust, and residue, with no damage or slipperiness post-cleaning. • Carpeted Floors: Must be free of all visible spots and stains that can be removed with heavy duty machinery and industrial-grade sanitation materials. • Restrooms: All surfaces must be visibly clean, sanitized, and free of odors, soap scum, and water spots. • Locker Rooms: All surfaces (lockers, benches, floors) must be visibly clean, sanitized, and free of dirt, grime, and odors. 2.0 Scope of Work The contractor shall provide all necessary labor, supervision, equipment, and supplies to perform a one- time deep cleaning of the specified facilities. The primary objective is to restore the floors and restrooms to a high standard of cleanliness. The locations included in this PWS are: • Fitness Center 1, 130 McChord Street, Bldg. 15, Washington, DC 20032 28,000 square • Fitness Center 2, 215 Enterprise Way, Bldg. 419, Washington, DC 20032 25,000 square feet • Aerobic Center, 38 Brookley Ave SW, Bldg. 38, Washington, DC 20032 20,000 square feet 3.0 Specific Tasks The contractor shall perform the following tasks: Contractor will be

provide all labor, materials, equipment, and supplies necessary to complete all work specified in this PWS. 5.0 Period of Performance The work shall be completed within a mutually agreed-upon timeframe, coordinated by Mr. Jumaine Gould. The Contractor shall perform deep-cleaning services over three (3) consective weekends, consisting of Saturday and Sunday work periods. The Government will allocate four (4) hours of deep-cleaning service per scheduled work period. The specific dates and start times for each deep- cleaning period will be established by the Government and provided to the Contractor after contract award. 6.0 Performance Requirements Summary The Government will evaluate the contractor's performance against the following standards. Performance Objective Performance Standard Hard Floor Cleaning Floors are free of all visible dirt, dust, grime, and scuff marks. Grout lines are clean. Corners and edges are free of debris. Carpet Cleaning Office carpets are free of all visible spots and stains that can be removed with heavy duty machinery and industrial-grade sanitation materials. Rubberized Flooring Cleaning Rubberized surfaces are clean, sanitized, and free of dirt, dust, and residue. The surface is not damaged or slippery post-cleaning. Equipment Relocation All

quipment Relocation All equipment is returned to its original location undamaged. The floor beneath is cleaned to the standard of the surrounding area. Restroom Sanitation All surfaces are visibly clean, sanitized, and free of odors, soap scum, and water spots. Toilets and urinals are cleaned inside and out. Locker Room Sanitation All surfaces (lockers, benches, floors) are visibly clean, sanitized, and free of dirt, grime, and odors. 7.0 Acceptance Criteria All work will be inspected by Mr. Jumaine Gould upon completion. The work shall be considered complete and accepted only when it fully complies with the performance standards and requirements outlined in (section 6.0). Any deficiencies identified during the inspection, including damage to equipment or facilities, must be corrected by the contractor at no additional cost to the Government within 24 hours of notification. ===== FILE: files/Attachment_2_Provisions_and_Clauses.pdf ===== DEPARTMENT OF the air force 11TH CONTRACTING SQUADRON WASHINGTON DC Applicable Provisions and Clauses JBAB Deep Cleaning Services Fitness Centers 1 & 2, and Aerobic Center FA706026Q00021 ATTACHMENT # 2 The following pages are the provisions and clauses for the posted solicitation. As used in this provision- Vendor Lock-In-The term vendor lock-in refers to a situation in which the Government’s ability to operate, maintain, or transition a system, data, software, or related capability is limited due to dependency on proprietary technologies, formats, or services controlled by a specific contractor. This includes restrictions on access to models, training data, source code, documentation, or technical interfaces that would prevent or burden the Government’s ability to transition to alternative solutions or providers. (b) Vendor Lock-In Mitigation. The Government requires that offers submitted in response to this solicitation that incorporate AI technologies include terms that reduce vendor lock-in risk, such as requirements regarding knowledge transfer, clear data and model portability practices, clear licensing terms, and pricing transparency. This applies to all prime contractors and subcontractors performing AI-related work under this contract and must be flowed down accordingly. DOSAR 65

The EV Program has been restructured into two (2) elements, Earth Venture Orbital (EVO)1 and Earth Venture Suborbital (EVS). This will be the ﬁrst solicitation in the EVO series and will be soliciting innovative, Principal Investigator (PI)-led, cost-capped investigations for operations in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). The solicitation will accept proposals using a wide range of development approaches, including, but not limited to, commercial best practices and NASA Procedural Requirement (NPR) 7120.5, NASA Space Flight Program and Project Management Requirements, Class D tailored development approaches per NASA SMD Policy Document (SPD) 48 (https://soma.larc.nasa.gov/standardao/ClassD.html). Details will be made available in the ﬁnal text, including any speciﬁc restrictions based on applicability of selected approaches. The solicitation will call for proposals for innovative PI-led Earth science investigations implemented by developing one or more (a) space-based instruments for integration on a NASA-provided platform/launch vehicle; (b) instrument(s) and spacecraft (i.e., complete observatory), including CubeSats, for integration on a NASA-provided launch vehicle; or (c) complete missions

NASA is looking for community feedback to establish the optimal PIMMC, considering NASA’s intent to prioritize (reduced) time-to-science, leverage commercial products/services, and accommodability (e.g., simplicity of interfaces for integration of an instrument on a NASA-provided platform/launch vehicle or for integration of a complete observatory on a NASA-provided launch vehicle). NASA may select one or more investigations based on the established PIMMC value and funding availability. Participation will be open to all categories of U.S. and non-U.S. organizations, including educational institutions, University Aﬃliated Research Centers (UARCs), industry, not-for-proﬁt organizations, Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs), NASA Centers, and other Government agencies. NASA has not approved the issuance of a solicitation, and this CA does not obligate NASA to issue the solicitation and solicit proposals. Commercial contracting approaches that bundle spacecraft, launch and operations are also welcome. Proposals that leverage capabilities or incorporate best practices from commercial ﬂeet operators are encouraged. NASA also encourages proposers to consider co-ﬂying with commercial ﬂeet or current NASA missions. NASA is also open to innovative partnering opportunities that may help achieve greater science objectives within the budgetary limits of this solicitation. The solicitation will focus on the PI’s ability to reduce the time-to-science. As such, NASA desires the launch of the investigation to occur within 3-4 years of authority to proceed with a goal of going from proposal receipt to selection in 6 months. Current planning is for the selection process to be done in one step, with the selected investigation proceeding directly into formulation. NASA also intends to require the PI to identify potential non- NASA funded partnerships for continued operations and data collection/processing after the prime mission.
